title: Cat Wu, product lead for Claude Code, has left Anthropic
content:
Cat Wu, a top product manager at Anthropic and one of a small group behind the launch of its blockbuster tool Claude Code, left the company on Friday.
Wu announced her departure on Tuesday afternoon on X, thanking the Claude Code team and its users and reflecting on the tool's progress. As the head of product for Claude Code, Wu served as one of the two top leaders and evangelists for the technology alongside its original creator, Boris Cherny.
Claude Code, under Wu and Cherny's leadership, turned into one of the most important products in the AI industry's history. The tech gave Anthropic the viral product it needed to boost its revenues and access more funding for compute, and it turned the company into a bigger rival for OpenAI.
Wu did not say what prompted her departure and did not immediately respond to requests for comment. She's leaving at a crucial moment for Anthropic, as it churns toward a gargantuan initial public offering later this month. The company confirmed her departure. Thariq Shihipar, who also worked on Claude Code, announced his own departure last month.
Wu joined Anthropic in summer 2024 and tested an early prototype of Claude Code. In Tuesday's post, she reminisced on that moment: "It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team."
Anthropic released the tool in research preview in February 2025, announcing it in a brief demo video that featured Wu and Cherny.
The two decamped to AI coding startup Cursor that summer, and then returned to Anthropic a couple of weeks later, The Information reported.
Wu and Cherny then oversaw Claude Code's meteoric rise, which ramped up at the end of 2025. The tool first grew popular as an automatic coder for software engineers, who suddenly had a product that could sprint through entire coding tasks. Tech giants' AI bills with Anthropic soared as more developers started burning through Claude tokens.
Wu also oversees Cowork, Anthropic's tool for non-coding work, which relies on the same AI models and handles knowledge work for non-software engineers.
In an interview on Lenny's Podcast in April, Wu described her role as figuring out the path to bring Claude Code to the "AGI-pilled" version that Cherny envisioned for the future — a reference to the industry term "artificial general intelligence."
In her role, Wu said she worked with marketing, sales, finance, and other teams, and hired some of Anthropic's product managers. She also regularly responded to user requests about Claude Code on social media.
One commenter wrote under her X post on Tuesday, "Are you gonna take that 6 months vacations now?"
Wu answered: "post agi!"

report.summary: Cat Wu, product lead for Anthropic's Claude Code, has left the company ahead of its planned IPO, marking a high-profile departure from a key product team.
report.background: Claude Code launched in a research preview in February 2025 and quickly became one of Anthropic's most important products, driving revenue, attracting compute funding, and positioning the company as a stronger rival to OpenAI. Cat Wu joined Anthropic in summer 2024 after testing an early prototype, and she co-led Claude Code's product strategy alongside creator Boris Cherny. The pair briefly left for AI coding startup Cursor that summer before returning to Anthropic. Under their leadership, Claude Code's adoption surged at the end of 2025, especially among software engineers who used it to automate coding tasks. Wu also oversaw Cowork, Anthropic's tool for non-coding knowledge work. Her exit comes as Anthropic prepares for a massive IPO and as competition for AI coding talent remains intense.
key_points: Wu announced her departure on X on Tuesday and left Anthropic on Friday. The company confirmed the exit, but Wu did not give a reason and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

As head of product for Claude Code, Wu was one of two top leaders and evangelists for the tool, working alongside original creator Boris Cherny. She also oversaw Cowork, Anthropic's tool for non-coding work.

The timing is sensitive: Anthropic is moving toward a huge IPO later this month. Another Claude Code staffer, Thariq Shihipar, also announced his departure last month, raising questions about talent retention.

Claude Code became a viral hit and a major revenue driver for Anthropic, helping it compete with OpenAI. Tech giants' AI bills with Anthropic soared as more developers burned through Claude tokens for coding tasks.

Wu and Cherny briefly left Anthropic for Cursor in summer 2025 before returning a couple of weeks later, highlighting the fierce competition for AI coding talent and the strategic importance of Claude Code.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Wu's departure is a reminder that talent retention is a major risk for Anthropic as it approaches a high-profile IPO. Claude Code is central to Anthropic's enterprise strategy, and leadership changes could affect product direction or customer confidence. For developers, Claude Code and Cowork remain key tools, but a shift in product leadership may change priorities, roadmap, or community engagement. Rivals like OpenAI, Cursor, and open-source coding agents may see an opening to attract users or talent. For regular users, immediate changes are unlikely, but the departure could influence how quickly new features arrive and how Anthropic balances coding versus broader knowledge-work tools. The IPO will likely increase scrutiny on Anthropic's product organization and growth story.
report.tools: To follow the space, watch Anthropic's Claude Code and Cowork for product updates, and Cursor as a competing AI coding environment. Open-source alternatives such as Aider, Cline, and OpenHands offer ways to experiment with AI-assisted coding locally or via APIs. Tracking Anthropic's IPO filings and developer forums can also reveal how leadership changes affect roadmap and pricing.
